# Test a finite-output implementation in the complete strong residual norm

2026-10-27 HST, E003/S169. Ordinary argument frozen before execution;
the initial receipt retains its exact pre-result text and arithmetic.
The previous turn bounded the complete source and associated operator
graph, but did not implement S_Q. Test the proposed implementation class
before assembling a large matrix: any linear map S_hat with output in a
fixed space of dimension at most one million, certified through

    beta_H=||B_H-A_Q S_hat||_(Et->H),
    H=L2(z^-4 dz), A_Q=(ell_Q+B)/N in its H realization.       (1)

The safe sufficient target is beta_H<=4.964e-32. A coefficient or action
rounding error cannot improve a lower bound valid for EVERY such output
map, even with exact coefficients. If its outputs are not in Dom(A_Q),
(1) is unavailable already. An adaptive method with input-dependent
output spaces, or an analytic infinite-rank solver, is outside this test.
This is not a test of the full physical inverse's existence.

## 1. Actual-domain fields, not arbitrary prescribed quantum sources

Keep the actual paired mass/log closure E_t, original period/scale,
complementary Dirac domains, common regulator, full angular/thermal sums,
contacts, cutoff transitions and regular bolt. Work on I=[.4,.6], where
all relevant coefficients are smooth. No operator or boundary is replaced.
Set M=1000001 and divide I into M disjoint cells of width h=.2/M.
On cell j let phi_j(z)=(1-x_j^2)^8 for |x_j|<1 and zero otherwise,
where x_j=2(z-center_j)/h. Let Q be the actual full seed polynomial and

    m=(Q'/z^4)', J=m phi'+2m' phi,
    xi=(QJ)'-z^4 m^2 phi,
    nu=xi/2+QJ/z, T=-xi-(QJ)'/2.                         (2)

Since mJ=(m^2 phi)', the full York moment is zero. Direct differentiation
gives the original York equation. J,xi,nu,T vanish outside their cell,
including every endpoint trace needed here. In particular the original
outer and bolt conditions hold, with zero mass/log coefficients on these
test directions. These compact directions lie INSIDE the actual domain;
they do not replace its nonzero phases or truncate physical matter modes.
The fields are C5 and have more than the required weak derivatives. Smooth
core approximation preserves the strict inequalities below. All cell
transitions are part of the fields and their derivative bounds.

Write xi=sum_(i=0)^2 a_i phi^(i). Exactly,

    a2=Qm, a1=Q'm+3Qm', a0=2(Qm')'-z^4m^2.              (3)

The corresponding nu and T coefficient arrays follow from (2), without
solving a new boundary problem. Qm has a positive minimum on I. Thus
the nonzero disjoint fields xi_j span an M-dimensional real space U_M.

## 2. Uniform bounds on this entire space

Let f_k be the EXACT L2(-1,1) norms of the derivatives of (1-x^2)^8,
k=0,...,5, computed by polynomial integration. Put w=2/h and

    D0=(inf_I a2) w^2 f2 - ||a1||inf w f1 - ||a0||inf f0.

For each cell, ||xi||_L2(dz)>=sqrt(h/2) D0; execute D0>0.
For any of the three coefficient arrays c_i for xi,nu,T and k<=3,

    N_k(c)=sum_i sum_(j=0)^k binom(k,j)
                  ||c_i^(j)||inf w^(i+k-j) f_(i+k-j),
    ||field^(k)||_L2(dz)/||xi||_H <= .6^2 N_k(c)/D0.       (4)

The same inequalities hold for every linear combination in U_M, since
supports are disjoint. For H derivative norms multiply (4) by .4^-2.
For xi itself use its exact H norm, not the loose k=0 bound.
All coefficient bounds are whole-interval enclosures, not samples.

The physical scalar Laplacian and gradient are exactly

    Deltabar xi=(z^2/beta)[Q xi''+(Q'-2Q/z)xi'],
    ||gradbar xi||_H^2=(1/beta) int Q z^-2 |xi'|^2 dz.

Using (4) gives upper constants L2,L1 for these two quantities per
unit H norm. Cell Dirichlet Poincare gives the LOWER constant

    ||gradbar xi||_H^2 >= g_low ||xi||_H^2,
    g_low=(inf_I Q)*.4^4*pi^2/(beta*.6^2*h^2).            (5)

No estimate on an arbitrary-source correction is used. The scalar test
in the original first equation is s=xi. The complete scalar energy obeys

    a(xi,xi)/N <= A_up ||xi||_H^2,
    A_up=6d L2^2+6.01 L1^2+24.01, d=D_R lambda.          (6)

The coefficients follow from the current exact scalar row and its fixed
curvature/coupling guards: ||K||<6.01 and
|2R4+48lambda0|/lambda<24.01. This is a global physical scalar test
with compact support, not a replacement of a^-1 by a scalar matrix.

Let tau_bar=tau/lambda, tau_min=inf_I tau_bar>0, and
t2=||Deltabar tau_bar||inf. Integrate the main mixed row ONCE:

    b_main(xi,xi)/N
      =4 int [C_v tau_bar xi^2+d tau_bar |gradbar xi|^2
                                    -(d/2)(Deltabar tau_bar)xi^2] dmu_H.

The COMPLETE nonleading mixed bound from the previous turn is
K_rest<1.683278e-27 in A x H. It includes all curvature, magnetic,
off-shell and nonlocal York-return terms, including their cross-cell
couplings. Consequently

    b(xi,xi)/N >= b_low ||xi||_H^2,
    b_low=4(C_v tau_min+d tau_min g_low-d t2/2)
                                                    -K_rest sqrt(A_up).

Execute b_low>0. Maximizing 2b(s,xi)/N-a(s,s)/N over the SINGLE scalar
direction s=c xi then proves the full coupled variational lower bound

    (B_H xi,xi)_H >= b_low^2/A_up ||xi||_H^2=:B_low||xi||_H^2. (7)

The exact full scalar inverse remains in B_H. Restricting its variational
maximization supplies a lower bound, not an approximate scalar solve.

## 3. Upper-bound the COMPLETE quantum energy before using dimension

A local classical energy alone cannot upper-bound E_t. Use the accepted
complete geodesic comparison ell_0 with |ell-ell_0|<=.0022 ell.
Its physical quantum logarithm, full common local restoration and all
state/thermal/boundary differences stay in the comparison and its error.

Evaluate ALL FOUR exact affine local densities (2)-(3) of
current-finite-local-action-assembly.md: Einstein/cosmological, magnetic,
additional R2 and Weyl. Use the six ORDINARY independent jets
(nu,nu',nu'',T,T',T''). This retains the off-shell density terms directly;
no unquantified chart-conversion reserve or stationarity assumption enters.
For each allocation alpha, interval differentiation of its displayed
density gives its symmetric Hessian matrix H_alpha(z). If C_alpha,ij
bounds |H_alpha,ij| on I, (4) gives

    E_local <= (1/beta) sum_alpha sum_ij
                            C_alpha,ij Ljet_i Ljet_j.    (8)

Here the off-diagonal terms are counted twice, exactly as in the quadratic
form v^t H v. The interval operation computes the second derivative, not
the Taylor coefficient divided by two. The negative physical action
factor is harmless for this absolute upper bound; beta is the ORIGINAL
conversion from I/W to ell/N. This deliberately conservative local bound
may discard beneficial cancellations only after retaining the full
two-row returned fields. Its looseness weakens, never strengthens, the
residual lower bound (11).

Add canonical a2, LLL and the shared bounded vacuum coefficient exactly
once, using (5)-(6) of current-canonical-heat-restoration-assembly.md.
With R=-Q'', Delta T=QT''+Q'T', their absolute quadratic bounds are
|beta2|[4Rmax^2 LT0^2+16Rmax LT0 LDelta+8LDelta^2],
|Gq/(6pi B_radius^2)| Qmax LT1^2, and U0 LT0^2,
respectively, all divided by beta. Set LDelta=Qmax LT2+Q1 LT1.
The vacuum value remains one bounded shared coefficient; it is not zero.

The fixed log z and F_eff retain their actual values; no scale is reset.
The original boundary Hessians vanish on (2), rather than being omitted
from the operator. This assembly is only an upper energy bound for the
test space, not a signed evaluation of the full residual.

The remaining positive geodesic form has the already proved complete
all-angular bound P_M[T]<=||X^3 T||^2/(525pi^2 M^4),
sum d_n/M_n^4<4C^2/q. The actual full flow retains trapped trajectories
and regular-bolt returns; the generator argument applies because these
compact C5 fields lie in Dom(X^3). With Qmax=||Q||inf, Q1,Q2 its
first two derivative bounds, and the T-jet constants from (4), set

    A=Qmax LT3, D=1.5 Q1 LT2+.5 Q2 LT1,
    E_geo=2(4C^2/q)/(525pi B_radius^2 beta)
                           *Qmax*(5A^2/8+1.5 A D+D^2).   (9)

This follows by angular integration of the exact third-flow derivative;
it bounds the ENTIRE positive logarithmic form, not selected frequencies.
Combining all terms and the actual retained-transport comparison gives

    ||xi||_Et^2 <= E_up ||xi||_H^2,
    E_up=(1+epsilon)/(1-.0022)
                       *(E_local+E_a2+E_LLL+E_vacuum+E_geo). (10)

Disjoint-support derivative norms bound every cross-cell quantum pairing
through (9), so (10) is uniform on U_M, not only its individual basis fields.

## 4. The actual finite-output residual lower bound

For a fixed output space of dimension at most M-1, choose nonzero
u in U_M orthogonal in H to its A_Q image. Then

    (u,(B_H-A_Q S_hat)u)_H=(u,B_H u)_H>=B_low||u||_H^2.

Cauchy--Schwarz and (10) prove

    beta_H >= B_low/sqrt(E_up).                          (11)

This uses the actual structured source B_H and both original equations.
It is not an arbitrary-source counterexample and does not assert failure
of the actual coupled inverse. The analogous full energy-dual test yields
only rho_S>=B_low/E_up. Compute BOTH bounds, their ratios to the actual
sufficient screens, and the resulting floor of the proposed strong-norm
upper estimator's complete source debit. Do not call that estimator floor

If (11) exceeds 4.964e-32, this rejects the SPECIFIED strong-residual
finite-output implementation at this rank, even with perfect arithmetic.
A weak lower bound below its screen is NOT a weak certificate or proof
of attainability. No degree, transport-depth or tail optimization is
authorized by that inconclusive comparison.

## 5. Execution and decision boundary

Execute the complete inequalities once with exact polynomial norm
integrals and 512-bit outward intervals, preserving every outcome.
The supporting arithmetic verifies this ordinary full-domain argument;
it neither implements a million-column solver nor evaluates the signed
quantum correction. The next method choice must use the resulting bounds.

The source regularity bound, P32, all accepted results and closed audit
remain unchanged. No mass-column, original geometric admission, nonlinear
existence/contraction, compatibility, matching, semiclassical validity/noise

The initial 512-bit execution is retained in

The last bound is over 207.22 times the sufficient 4.964e-32 screen for

Through the existing strong-residual conversion and complete 12-term

The mathematical loss is explicit: the complete B_H source has a positive

The first required continuum implication for this test is membership of

"""Full-source finite-output strong-residual test; not an inverse implementation."""
from pathlib import Path
from hashlib import sha256
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from fractions import Fraction
from math import comb
import argparse
import json
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
STEM = 'current-strong-residual-rank-test'
RUNTIME = ROOT / 'evidence/current-coupled-mass-adjoint-runtime.json'
runtime = json.loads(RUNTIME.read_bytes())
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(runtime['packages']['flint']['root']).parent))
from flint import arb, ctx

INPUTS = [
    'notes/'+STEM+'.md', 'checks/current_strong_residual_rank_test.py',
    'notes/current-structured-source-graph-test.md',
    'notes/current-finite-local-action-assembly.md',
    'notes/current-canonical-heat-restoration-assembly.md',
    'notes/current-seed-full-hessian-realization.md',
    'notes/current-quartic-ritz-rank-test.md',
    'notes/current-geodesic-two-sided-remainder.md',
    'evidence/current-structured-source-graph-test.json',
    'evidence/current-geodesic-two-sided-remainder.json',
    'evidence/current-canonical-heat-restoration-assembly.json',
    'evidence/current-spatial-inverse-output-test.json',
    'evidence/current-coupled-mass-adjoint-runtime.json',
]
BASELINE = Path('C:/Users/dfred/AppData/Local/Temp/s169-weak-response-execution-baseline.json')


def digest(p):
    return sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def dec(v):
    d = v['decimal_enclosure']
    return arb(int(d['mid']), int(d['rad']))*arb(10)**int(d['exponent'])


def enc(v):
    m, r, e = v.mid_rad_10exp(60)
    return {'ball': v.str(40), 'decimal_enclosure':
            {'mid': str(m), 'rad': str(r), 'exponent': str(e)}}


def receipt(stem, status='passed'):
    obj = json.loads((ROOT/'evidence'/(stem+'.json')).read_bytes())
    run = obj.get('runs', [obj])[-1]
    assert run['status'] == status
    return run


def pick(run, kind):
    return next(x for x in run['numerics'] if x['kind'] == kind)


def add(*ps):
    out = {}
    for p in ps:
        for k, v in p.items():
            out[k] = out.get(k, arb(0))+v
    return {k: v for k, v in out.items() if not v.is_zero()}


def scale(p, x):
    return {k: v*x for k, v in p.items()}


def mul(p, q):
    out = {}
    for i, a in p.items():
        for j, b in q.items():
            out[i+j] = out.get(i+j, arb(0))+a*b
    return out


def diff(p):
    return {k-1: k*v for k, v in p.items() if k}


def shift(p, n):
    return {k+n: v for k, v in p.items()}


def value(p, z):
    return sum((v*z**k for k, v in p.items()), arb(0))


def fadd(*cs):
    return [add(*(c[i] for c in cs if i < len(c))) for i in range(max(map(len, cs)))]


def fscale(c, x):
    return [scale(p, x) for p in c]


def fmul(c, p):
    return [mul(q, p) for q in c]


def fdiff(c):
    return fadd([diff(p) for p in c], [{}]+c)


class Jet:
    """Value, two directional derivatives, mixed derivative: outward Arb."""
    def __init__(self, v=0, i=0, j=0, ij=0):
        self.v, self.i, self.j, self.ij = map(arb, [v, i, j, ij])

    @staticmethod
    def lift(x):
        return x if isinstance(x, Jet) else Jet(x)

    def __add__(self, x):
        x = Jet.lift(x)
        return Jet(self.v+x.v, self.i+x.i, self.j+x.j, self.ij+x.ij)
    __radd__ = __add__

    def __neg__(self):
        return Jet(-self.v, -self.i, -self.j, -self.ij)

    def __sub__(self, x):
        return self+-Jet.lift(x)

    def __rsub__(self, x):
        return Jet.lift(x)+-self

    def __mul__(self, x):
        x = Jet.lift(x)
        return Jet(self.v*x.v, self.i*x.v+self.v*x.i,
                   self.j*x.v+self.v*x.j,
                   self.ij*x.v+self.i*x.j+self.j*x.i+self.v*x.ij)
    __rmul__ = __mul__

    def __truediv__(self, x):
        return self*(1/arb(x))

    def __pow__(self, n):
        assert isinstance(n, int) and n >= 0
        out = Jet(1)
        for _ in range(n):
            out = out*self
        return out

    def exp(self):
        ev = self.v.exp()
        return Jet(ev, ev*self.i, ev*self.j, ev*(self.ij+self.i*self.j))


def local_hessian(i, j, z, Q, Q1, Q2, C, B2, q):
    v = [Jet(0, int(i == k), int(j == k)) for k in range(6)]
    n, n1, n2, t, t1, t2 = v
    phi, phi1, phi2 = -z.log()+n, -1/z+n1, 1/z**2+n2
    L = -Q2-2*(Q*t2+Q1*t1)
    M = Q*phi2+Q1*phi1
    P = Q*phi1**2
    D = L-6*M-6*P
    en2, en4, et2, etm2 = (2*n).exp(), (4*n).exp(), (2*t).exp(), (-2*t).exp()
    LE = en2*D/(2*z**2)+en2*et2/(C*z**2)+3*arb(2000)**-10*B2/C*en4*et2/z**4
    LEM = -arb.pi()*q**2*arb(2000)**8/(C*B2)*et2
    LR = 8*arb.pi()*arb('1e22')/(C*B2)*(4*et2+4*C*D+C*C*etm2*D**2)
    bracket = phi*L**2/60+L*M/30-M**2/10+L*P/30-7*M*P/90-7*P**2/180
    LW = (C*C*etm2*bracket-C*phi*L/18+(arb(1)/15-q*q/3)*phi*et2-C*P/18)/(2*arb.pi()*C*B2)
    return dict(Einstein=LE.ij, magnetic=LEM.ij, R2=LR.ij, Weyl=LW.ij)


def execute():
    ctx.prec = 512
    assert digest(Path(sys.executable)) == runtime['python_sha256']
    for pkg in runtime['packages'].values():
        for name, expected in pkg['files'].items():
            assert digest(Path(pkg['root'])/name) == expected
    geo = receipt('current-geodesic-two-sided-remainder')
    ep = pick(geo, 'actual_seed_correlated_endpoint')
    gp = pick(geo, 'actual_finite_seed_two_sided_parameters')
    rc = pick(receipt('current-canonical-heat-restoration-assembly'), 'common_restoration_coefficients')
    sc = receipt('current-structured-source-graph-test',
                 'source_graph_bound_checked_complete_application_unresolved')['constants']
    sp = receipt('current-spatial-inverse-output-test',
                 'error_estimator_test_passed_signed_action_unresolved')['result']['constants']
    Q = {k: dec(v) for k, v in zip([0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], ep['Q_coefficients'])}
    C, B2, lam = dec(gp['C']), dec(gp['B2']), dec(gp['lambda_value'])
    beta, q = Q[0], dec(gp['q'])
    epsilon = dec(sp['epsilon'])
    d, Cv, Krest = dec(sc['d']), dec(sc['C_v']), dec(sc['mixed_remainders_total'])
    assert beta.overlaps(lam*B2/C) and arb('.99') < dec(ep['z_h'])
    assert 0 < epsilon < arb('1.227e-74')
    ds, x = Q[6]*C, lam*B2
    assert abs(ds) < arb('8.6e-19')
    m = diff(shift(diff(Q), -4))
    J = [scale(diff(m), 2), m]
    QJ = fmul(J, Q)
    Ap = fdiff(QJ)
    xi = fadd(Ap, [scale(shift(mul(m, m), 4), -1)])
    nu = fadd(fscale(xi, arb(1)/2), [shift(p, -1) for p in QJ])
    T = fadd(fscale(xi, -1), fscale(Ap, -arb(1)/2))
    # The original York differential equation as a Laurent/jet identity.
    qqjp = fmul(fdiff(J), mul(Q, Q))
    rhs = fmul(fadd([shift(scale(p, 4), -1) for p in xi], fscale(fdiff(xi), -1)), Q)
    york = fadd(fscale(fdiff(qqjp), -1), [shift(scale(p, 4), -1) for p in qqjp], fscale(rhs, -1))
    assert all(v.contains(0) for p in york for v in p.values())
    moment = fadd(fmul(J, m), fscale(fdiff([mul(m, m)]), -1))
    assert all(v.contains(0) for p in moment for v in p.values())

    # Exact polynomial integration for each bump-derivative norm.
    p = {2*i: Fraction((-1)**i*comb(8, i)) for i in range(9)}
    f, exact = [], []
    for k in range(6):
        moment2 = sum((a*b*Fraction(2, i+j+1) for i, a in p.items()
                       for j, b in p.items() if (i+j) % 2 == 0), Fraction(0))
        assert moment2 > 0
        exact.append(str(moment2))
        f.append((arb(moment2.numerator)/moment2.denominator).sqrt())
        p = {i-1: i*a for i, a in p.items() if i}

    a, b, cells = arb('.4'), arb('.6'), 128
    # The rational endpoints .4+j/(640) are represented by interval arithmetic.
    intervals = []
    for j in range(cells):
        lo, hi = a+(b-a)*j/cells, a+(b-a)*(j+1)/cells
        intervals.append(lo.union(hi))
    def sup(p):
        return max(value(p, z).abs_upper() for z in intervals)
    def inf(p):
        return min(value(p, z).lower() for z in intervals)
    bounds = {}
    for name, c in [('xi', xi), ('nu', nu), ('T', T)]:
        bounds[name] = []
        for ci in c:
            row, cur = [], ci
            for j in range(4):
                row.append(sup(cur))
                cur = diff(cur)
            bounds[name].append(row)
    Mdim = 1000001
    h = (b-a)/Mdim
    w = 2/h
    a2low = inf(xi[2])
    D0 = a2low*w*w*f[2]-bounds['xi'][1][0]*w*f[1]-bounds['xi'][0][0]*f[0]
    assert a2low > 0 and D0 > 0
    dz = {}
    for name, cs in bounds.items():
        dz[name] = []
        for k in range(4):
            nk = sum((comb(k, j)*cs[i][j]*w**(i+k-j)*f[i+k-j]
                      for i in range(3) for j in range(k+1)), arb(0))
            dz[name].append(b*b*nk/D0)
    RH1, RH2 = dz['xi'][1]/a**2, dz['xi'][2]/a**2
    Qmax, Qmin, Q1max, Q2max = sup(Q), inf(Q), sup(diff(Q)), sup(diff(diff(Q)))
    drift = add(diff(Q), scale(shift(Q, -1), -2))
    L1 = Qmax.sqrt()*b/beta.sqrt()*RH1
    L2 = b*b/beta*(Qmax*RH2+sup(drift)*RH1)
    glow = Qmin*a**4*arb.pi()**2/(beta*b*b*h*h)
    tau = {4: (1+3*x+ds)/x, 5: -5*ds/x, 6: arb(9)/2*ds/x}
    taulow = inf(tau)
    Dt = scale(shift(add(mul(Q, diff(diff(tau))), mul(drift, diff(tau))), 2), 1/beta)
    t2 = sup(Dt)
    # Check the scalar coefficient guards used in the ordinary upper bound.
    Rbar = {0: arb(-12), 5: 4*ds/x, 6: -6*ds/x}
    ee = lam/(60*arb.pi())
    Kupper = 6+(2*d+11*ee/6)*sup(Rbar)+(22*ee/3)*7
    Vupper = sup(add(scale(Rbar, 2), {0: 48*arb(2000)**-10/lam}))
    assert Kupper < arb('6.01') and Vupper < arb('24.01')
    Aup = 6*d*L2**2+arb('6.01')*L1**2+arb('24.01')
    blow = 4*(Cv*taulow+d*taulow*glow-d*t2/2)-Krest*Aup.sqrt()
    assert Qmin > 0 and taulow > 0 and blow > 0
    Blow = blow**2/Aup

    # Complete affine local Hessians on an interval cover; no point sampling.
    labels = ['Einstein', 'magnetic', 'R2', 'Weyl']
    matrices = {name: [[arb(0) for _ in range(6)] for _ in range(6)] for name in labels}
    for z in intervals:
        q0, q1, q2 = value(Q,z), value(diff(Q),z), value(diff(diff(Q)),z)
        for i in range(6):
            for j in range(i,6):
                co = local_hessian(i,j,z,q0,q1,q2,C,B2,q)
                for name in labels:
                    bound = co[name].abs_upper()
                    matrices[name][i][j] = max(matrices[name][i][j],bound)
                    matrices[name][j][i] = matrices[name][i][j]
    jets = dz['nu'][:3]+dz['T'][:3]
    local = {name: sum((mat[i][j]*jets[i]*jets[j] for i in range(6) for j in range(6)),arb(0))/beta
             for name,mat in matrices.items()}
    lt0, lt1, lt2, lt3 = dz['T']
    ld = Qmax*lt2+Q1max*lt1
    ea2 = dec(rc['beta2']).abs_upper()*(4*Q2max**2*lt0**2+16*Q2max*lt0*ld+8*ld**2)/beta
    elll = dec(rc['LLL_Hessian_coefficient']).abs_upper()*Qmax*lt1**2/beta
    evac = dec(rc['vacuum_coefficient_upper'])*lt0**2/beta
    A, D = Qmax*lt3, arb('1.5')*Q1max*lt2+Q2max*lt1/2
    s2 = 4*C*C/q
    integraltest = 2*C*C*(q+2)/(q+1)**2+2*C*C/(q+1)
    assert integraltest < s2
    egeo = 2*s2/(525*arb.pi()*B2*beta)*Qmax*(arb(5)/8*A*A+arb('1.5')*A*D+D*D)
    Eup = (1+epsilon)/(1-arb('.0022'))*(sum(local.values(),arb(0))+ea2+elll+evac+egeo)
    stronglower, weaklower = Blow/Eup.sqrt(), Blow/Eup
    strongscreen, weakscreen = arb('4.964e-32'), arb('4.989e-32')
    multiplier = dec(sc['strong_residual_to_COMPLETE_residual_multiplier'])
    weak_application = dec(sc['energy_dual_residual_to_application_multiplier'])*weakscreen
    weak_debit = multiplier*dec(sc['c_H']).sqrt()*weakscreen
    constants = dict(M=arb(Mdim), h=h, D0=D0, a2_lower=a2low, Q_lower=Qmin,
                     tau_lower=taulow, scalar_K_upper=Kupper, scalar_V_upper=Vupper,
                     scalar_L1_upper=L1, scalar_L2_upper=L2, gradient_squared_lower=glow,
                     scalar_energy_upper=Aup, mixed_main_lower=blow+Krest*Aup.sqrt(),
                     mixed_remainder_debit=Krest*Aup.sqrt(), complete_mixed_lower=blow,
                     complete_B_lower=Blow, canonical_a2_upper=ea2,
                     canonical_LLL_upper=elll, shared_vacuum_upper=evac,
                     full_angular_sum_upper=s2, complete_nonlocal_energy_upper=egeo,
                     complete_Et_energy_upper=Eup,
                     strong_residual_lower_bound=stronglower,
                     energy_dual_residual_lower_bound=weaklower,
                     strong_ratio_to_sufficient_screen=stronglower/strongscreen,
                     weak_ratio_to_sufficient_screen=weaklower/weakscreen,
                     strong_estimator_complete_source_debit_floor=multiplier*stronglower,
                     strong_debit_floor_to_ENTIRE_residual_screen=multiplier*stronglower/arb('1e-30'),
                     conditional_complete_source_allocation=multiplier*strongscreen,
                     conditional_weak_application_error_NOT_attained=weak_application,
                     conditional_weak_source_debit_NOT_attained=weak_debit)
    constants.update({'local_'+k+'_energy_upper':v for k,v in local.items()})
    return dict(constants={k:enc(v) for k,v in constants.items()},
                exact_bump_derivative_squared_norms=exact,
                ordinary_jet_norm_comparisons={k:[enc(x) for x in v] for k,v in dz.items()},
                local_coefficient_absolute_matrices={k:[[enc(x) for x in row] for row in mat] for k,mat in matrices.items()},
                interval_cover_cells=cells, maximum_fixed_output_dimension=Mdim-1,
                original_York_identity_checked=True, compact_York_moment_checked=True,
                strong_finite_output_screen_rejected=bool(stronglower > strongscreen),
                weak_test_rejects_screen=bool(weaklower > weakscreen),
                actual_S_application_error=None, actual_K_application_error=None,
                actual_complete_numerical_residual=None,
                certifies_inverse_or_wormhole_nonexistence=False)


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--output', default='evidence/'+STEM+'.json')
    args=parser.parse_args()
    output=ROOT/args.output
    if output.exists():
        raise RuntimeError('Receipts are immutable; choose a fresh output path.')
    protected=json.loads(BASELINE.read_bytes())
    verify=lambda: all(digest(Path(p))==h for p,h in protected.items())
    assert verify()
    before={p:digest(ROOT/p) for p in INPUTS}
    data={'started_utc':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
          'previous_goal_turn':'No progress: requested email recheck supplied no new bound.',
          'input_sha256_before':before,
          'ordinary_argument_utf8':(ROOT/INPUTS[0]).read_text(encoding='utf-8'),
          'arithmetic_source_utf8':Path(__file__).read_text(encoding='utf-8')}
    try:
        data['result']=execute()
        data['status']='finite_output_estimator_test_executed_full_application_unresolved'
    except Exception as exc:
        data['status']='failed'
        data['error']=repr(exc)
        raise
    finally:
        data['input_sha256_after']={p:digest(ROOT/p) for p in INPUTS}
        data['inputs_unchanged']=before==data['input_sha256_after']
        data['protected_paths_unchanged']=verify()
        data['protected_path_count']=len(protected)
        data['finished_utc']=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        output.write_text(json.dumps(data,indent=2)+'\n',encoding='utf-8',newline='\n')
    assert data['inputs_unchanged'] and data['protected_paths_unchanged']
    for k,v in data['result']['constants'].items():
        print(k+': '+v['ball'])
    print('Receipt: '+str(output))


if __name__=='__main__':
    main()
